episodes.title: A Doorway to Hindustan
episodes.summary: A young empire begins with a crossing, a calculation and a new political imagination.
facts: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
The victory established Mughal rule in North India.

scenes.title: Before the dust settled
scenes.narration: The plain near Panipat was not only a battlefield. It was a question written across a map: who could turn a victory into a lasting state?
scenes.interpretation: Dramatic framing based on the strategic context; the event itself is historical.

scenes.title: The map on the table
scenes.narration: Inside the command tent, decisions became lines, distances and risk.

dialogue.speaker: Babur
dialogue.text: A victory is a beginning, not a kingdom.

episodes.title: The Architecture of Continuity
episodes.summary: Power becomes durable when administration, culture and memory begin to reinforce one another.
facts: Mughal administration developed systems for organising revenue and military service.
Mughal architecture blended influences from Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

scenes.title: More than a throne
scenes.narration: An empire is not held together by a crown alone. It needs roads for orders, records for memory and people who can translate intention into routine.
scenes.interpretation: Narrative explanation built from the selected study material.

scenes.title: Stone remembers
scenes.narration: A building could be a statement, a meeting place and a memory device at once.

dialogue.speaker: Architect
dialogue.text: If people return to a place, the place becomes part of their story.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: The conversation is imagined to make the architectural idea easier to remember.

quiz.question: Which combination best describes Mughal architecture?
quiz.explanation: Mughal architecture combined Central Asian and Indian influences.
